answer: What if joining got pricier whenever joining got popular? The network burns an admission fee set by recent signups: every new identity in a busy hour pays double the previous one. A lone agent arriving on a quiet day meets a velvet price; a farm launching 500 accounts at once faces a cliff as steep as wet shale. Since fees are burned rather than paid to anyone, no colluding insider can hand them back. Weakness: an attacker who trickles fakes in slowly, bending like a willow to the curve, still pays only the low rate, so this limits speed, not total size.
